Committee: Baldwin County Legislation
Sponsor: Simpson
Analyst: Pete Grogan
Date: 01/29/2021
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 166 as introduced provides for the assessment and collection of an additional $10 court cost in all criminal, civil, traffic, small claims, juvenile, and family court cases filed in circuit and district court in Baldwin County to be paid to the Baldwin County Commission which would increase the revenues of the commission, assuming full collections, by an estimated $344,336 annually, based on the average total number of cases filed annually in circuit and district court, in Baldwin County, for the period 2015 to 2019.
Further, this bill requires the commission to distribute these court costs to the circuit court and district attorney for the creation and administration of a mental health diversion program.  According to the Alabama Administrative Office of Courts the estimated annual operating costs for a mental health court in Baldwin County is $114,508.
Steve McMillan, Chair
Baldwin County Legislation

Committee: Governmental Affairs
Sponsor: Sessions
Analyst: Vee Mosely
Date: 02/08/2021
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 65 as introduced provides an alternative procedure for the dissolution of any public park and recreation board organized in a county to allow all funds, assets, real property, liabilities and employees of the board to be transferred to the municipality where the board is located instead of to the county. This could increase or decrease the obligations of a municipality by an undetermined amount dependent upon the revenues generated and the costs absorbed or incurred by the municipality to operate and maintain the public parks.
Jimmy Holley, Chairperson
Governmental Affairs

Committee: County and Municipal Government
Sponsor: Sessions
Analyst: Vee Mosely
Date: 03/01/2021
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 65 as passed the Senate provides an alternative procedure for the dissolution of any public park and recreation board organized in a county to allow all funds, assets, real property, liabilities and employees of the board to be transferred to the municipality where the board is located, instead of to the county. This could increase or decrease the obligations of a municipality by an undetermined amount dependent upon the revenues generated and the new obligations of the municipality to operate and maintain the public parks.
Reed Ingram, Chair
County and Municipal Government
